Mean Pairwise and Mean Nearest Taxon Distance

Source: R/phylo_structure.r
mpd.Rd

How closely related the taxa in each sample are, along a phylogeny (or any dissimilarity among the taxa): the mean phylogenetic distance between pairs of the sample's taxa (MPD), or from each taxon to its nearest relative in the sample (MNTD) (Webb 2000; Webb et al. 2002). MPD responds to structure deep in the tree, MNTD to structure near its tips. The weighted_* forms weight each taxon by its abundance. To test them against a null model (NRI and NTI), see mpd_ses().

Usage

mpd(counts, tree = NULL, taxa_dm = NULL, margin = 1L, cpus = n_cpus())

weighted_mpd(counts, tree = NULL, taxa_dm = NULL, margin = 1L, cpus = n_cpus())

mntd(counts, tree = NULL, taxa_dm = NULL, margin = 1L, cpus = n_cpus())

weighted_mntd(
  counts,
  tree = NULL,
  taxa_dm = NULL,
  margin = 1L,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of non-negative abundances (samples \(\times\) taxa, see margin), or any of the other objects listed in "Input Types". Values need not be integers: mpd() and mntd() use only presence, and the weighted forms only relative abundances. The taxa must have names, to match them to the tips of tree or the labels of taxa_dm.

tree

A phylo object with branch lengths (none negative or missing), whose tips include every taxon of counts (see read_tree()). Tips that aren't taxa of counts are ignored. Can be omitted if a tree is embedded with the counts object or as attr(counts, 'tree'). Distances are path lengths along the tree (patristic distances), as from ape::cophenetic.phylo(). The tree may be unrooted, or have polytomies or nodes with one child: none of these change path lengths.

taxa_dm

Instead of tree: the dissimilarities among the taxa, as a dist object or symmetric matrix (picante's dis, which may be functional-trait distances, for instance). Labels are matched to the taxa of counts; without labels, rows are taken in the order of counts' taxa. An embedded tree is ignored when taxa_dm is given.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), is the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it. Results are the same for any cpus.

Value

A numeric vector with one value per sample, named by sample. A sample with fewer than two taxa is NA.

Details

For a sample with taxa \(i = 1 \ldots S\), abundances \(x_i\) (total \(W\)), and distances \(d_{ij}\):

  • MPD: \(\sum_{i<j} d_{ij} / (S(S-1)/2)\), the mean over pairs of distinct taxa.

  • Weighted MPD: \(\sum_{i,j} x_i x_j d_{ij} / W^2\), the mean distance between two individuals drawn at random, with replacement, so that pairs within a taxon count too (at distance 0). This is picante's and phylocom's definition.

  • MNTD: \(\sum_i m_i / S\), with \(m_i = \min_{j \ne i} d_{ij}\).

  • Weighted MNTD: \(\sum_i x_i m_i / W\).

The weighted forms are unchanged by scaling a sample, so counts and proportions give the same values. "Weighted" here means weighting by abundance; it is not the weighting of weighted_unifrac().

These are also alpha diversity metrics: alpha_div(counts, 'mpd', tree = tree), and likewise 'weighted_mpd', 'mntd' and 'weighted_mntd'.

Speed and memory

With a tree, no taxa \(\times\) taxa matrix is formed. Each sample's taxa are sorted into the tree's preorder, and the tree's lowest common ancestors of neighbours (found in constant time from a table built once) give the part of the tree that spans them, with at most \(2S - 1\) nodes; MPD and MNTD are one or two passes over it. Each sample takes time proportional to \(S \log S\), however large the tree. With taxa_dm, each sample reads its \(S^2\) distances. Results are identical for any number of cpus.

Differences from picante

Values agree with picante 1.8.4's mpd() and mntd() (with dis = cophenetic(tree) and abundance.weighted set to match) to about \(10^{-12}\). picante computes cophenetic(tree) first, a dense matrix of every pair of tips (3.2 GB for 20,000 tips); mpd() reads the tree directly. phylocom's comstruct gives MNTD 0, not NA, for a sample with one taxon.

Same names in other packages

picante::mpd() and picante::mntd() share these names (taking samp, dis and abundance.weighted); whichever package was attached last masks the other's. Write ecodive::mpd() to be sure. PhyloMeasures::mpd.query() computes the unweighted MPD.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Webb, C. O. (2000). Exploring the phylogenetic structure of ecological communities: an example for rain forest trees. American Naturalist, 156(2), 145-155. doi:10.1086/303378

Webb, C. O., Ackerly, D. D., McPeek, M. A., & Donoghue, M. J. (2002). Phylogenies and community ecology. Annual Review of Ecology and Systematics, 33, 475-505. doi:10.1146/annurev.ecolsys.33.010802.150448

Kembel, S. W., Cowan, P. D., Helmus, M. R., Cornwell, W. K., Morlon, H., Ackerly, D. D., Blomberg, S. P., & Webb, C. O. (2010). Picante: R tools for integrating phylogenies and ecology. Bioinformatics, 26(11), 1463-1464. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btq166

See also

mpd_ses() for NRI and NTI; faith(); alpha_div(); read_tree().

Other Phylogenetic metrics: faith(), generalized_unifrac(), mpd_ses(), normalized_unifrac(), philr_distance(), unweighted_unifrac(), variance_adjusted_unifrac(), weighted_unifrac()

Examples

    mpd(ex_counts, ex_tree)
#>   Saliva     Gums     Nose    Stool 
#> 92.16667 81.40000 79.06667 85.80000 
    weighted_mpd(ex_counts, ex_tree)
#>   Saliva     Gums     Nose    Stool 
#> 44.31146 16.49659 31.26699  1.43670 
    mntd(ex_counts, ex_tree)
#>   Saliva     Gums     Nose    Stool 
#> 74.50000 58.00000 52.66667 60.20000 
    weighted_mntd(ex_counts, ex_tree)
#>    Saliva      Gums      Nose     Stool 
#>  69.38261  34.36795  35.17606 103.64390 

    # The same through alpha_div().
    alpha_div(ex_counts, 'weighted_mntd', tree = ex_tree)
#>    Saliva      Gums      Nose     Stool 
#>  69.38261  34.36795  35.17606 103.64390 

    # Distances between (made-up) trait values instead of a tree.
    traits <- data.frame(
      row.names = colnames(ex_counts),
      gram_pos  = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1),
      size      = c(0.8, 1.5, 0.7, 1.2, 0.9, 1.0) )
    mpd(ex_counts, taxa_dm = dist(traits))
#>    Saliva      Gums      Nose     Stool 
#> 0.8179849 0.7345747 0.6896271 0.7734185
